'''Kurt H. Becker''' is an American physicist and entrepreneur.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.crainsnewyork.com/article/20150428/TECHNOLOGY/150429854/image-recognition-startup-becomes-50th-to-graduate-from-nyu-poly | title=Image-recognition startup becomes 50th to graduate from NYU Poly| author=Matthew Flamm| date=April 28, 2015| publisher=Crain’s New York| access-date=October 7, 2015}}</ref> His research focuses on experimental [[Atomic physics|atomic]], [[chemical physics|chemical]], and [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physics]].<ref name=epjb>{{cite web| url=http://epjb.epj.org/epjd-news/426-kurt-becker-to-lead-the-plasma-physics-sections-of-epj-d | title=Kurt Becker to lead the plasma physics sections of EPJ D| date=July 10, 2009| publisher=EPJ| access-date=October 7, 2015}}</ref> He is vice dean of research, innovation, and entrepreneurship at [[New York University Polytechnic School of Engineering]].<ref name=scientific>{{cite web| url=http://www.scientificamerican.com/article/aircraft-cargo-bomb-security/ | title=Exposing the Weakest Link: As Airline Passenger Security Tightens, Bombers Target Cargo Holds| date=November 2, 2010| author=Larry Greenemeier| publisher=Scientific American| access-date=October 7, 2015}}</ref><ref name=poly>{{cite web| url=https://engineering.nyu.edu/news/kurt-becker-receives-honorary-degree-university-innsbruck-austria| title=Kurt Becker Receives Honorary Degree From the University of Innsbruck, Austria| date=March 19, 2007| publisher=NYU Tandon School of Engineering| access-date=May 20, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=http://observer.com/2015/06/entrepreneurial-veterans-turn-their-back-burner-ideas-into-realities-with-nyu-program/ | title=Entrepreneurial Veterans Turn Their Back Burner Ideas Into Realities With NYU Program| author=Sage Lazzaro| date=June 12, 2015| publisher=Observer| access-date=October 7, 2015}}</ref> Becker holds seven patents regarding the generation and maintenance of atmospheric-pressure plasmas and their application.<ref name=aertc>{{cite web| url=http://observer.com/2015/06/entrepreneurial-veterans-turn-their-back-burner-ideas-into-realities-with-nyu-program/ | title=Advanced Energy Conference Solutions to a Global Crisis| publisher=Advanced Energy Research & Technology Center| access-date=October 7, 2015| date=2015-06-12}}</ref>

==Career==
In 1984, Becker began working at [[Lehigh University]]. He was head of the physics and [[engineering physics]] department, as well as associate director of the center for environmental systems at [[Stevens Institute of Technology]]. In 2001, he received the Thomas Alva Edison Patent Award from the [[Research and Development Council of New Jersey]].<ref>{{cite web| url=http://engineering.nyu.edu/people/kurt-h-becker| title=Kurt H. Becker| publisher=NYU Polytechnic School of Engineering| access-date=October 7, 2015}}</ref> Becker joined [[New York University Polytechnic School of Engineering]] in March 2007 when he was appointed associate provost for research and technology initiatives and dean of sciences and arts.<ref name=poly/> Becker oversees the NYU Incubator programs which support startup companies, including ACRE, the NYC clean-tech incubator, and NYU's first incubator at Varick St. in lower Manhattan.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://issuu.com/nyupoly/docs/cable_fall2013| title=Sowing the Seeds for Collaborative Research| date=2013| publisher=Cable| access-date=October 7, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.crainsnewyork.com/article/20150626/REAL_ESTATE/150629901/new-nyu-polytechnic-incubator-planned-at-former-brooklyn-industrial| title=New NYU Polytechnic incubator planned at former Brooklyn industrial complex| author=Daniel Geiger| date=June 26, 2015| publisher=Crain's New York Business| access-date=October 7, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=http://engineering.nyu.edu/business/incubators| title=Incubators| publisher=NYU Polytechnic School of Engineering| access-date=October 7, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=http://engineering.nyu.edu/business/incubators/faculty-engineers-in-residence| title=Faculty Engineers in Residence| publisher=NYU Polytechnic School of Engineering| access-date=October 7, 2015}}</ref>

In July 2009, Becker was appointed the third editor-in-chief of [[The European Physical Journal D|The European Physical Journal D: Atomic, Molecular, Optical and Plasma Physics]] to work with Franco Gianturco and [[Claude Fabre]]. His focus at the journal was low-temperature plasma physics.<ref name=epjb/>
Becker is a consultant for Ionicon Analytik, a gas analysis instrument company in Austria.<ref name=scientific/> He is also a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and the [[National Academy of Inventors]].<ref name=epjb/><ref name=press>{{cite web| url=http://engineering.nyu.edu/press-release/2013/12/09/kurt-h-becker-named-fellow-national-academy-inventors| title=Kurt H. Becker Named A Fellow of the National Academy of Inventors| date=December 9, 2013| publisher=NYU Polytechnic School of Engineering| access-date=October 7, 2015| archive-date=March 5, 2016| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305010025/http://engineering.nyu.edu/press-release/2013/12/09/kurt-h-becker-named-fellow-national-academy-inventors| url-status=dead}}</ref> Becker has also received the SASP Erwin Scroedinger Medal of the [[University of Innsbruck]].<ref name=press/>

==Research==
Becker focuses on the experimental and theoretical study of electron-driven processes in plasmas. Becker was part of a group of scientists leading the research on the determination of ionization cross sections of atoms and molecules. Their research worked toward the understanding of the [[charge carrier]] formation in plasmas.<ref>{{cite journal| title=Calculated electron ionization cross sections of the alkali atoms and the hydrogen spin ionization asymmetry|author1=Hans Deutsch |author2=Kurt Becker | doi=10.1140/epjd/e2014-50688-x| volume=69| journal=The European Physical Journal D|year = 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal| url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/222133663| title=Theoretical determination of absolute electron-impact ionization cross sections of molecules| journal=International Journal of Mass Spectrometry| volume=197| issue=1–3| pages=37–69|author1=H. Deutsch |author2=Kurt Becker |author3=Sonia Purin |author4=Tilmann D Mark | access-date=October 7, 2015| doi=10.1016/S1387-3806(99)00257-2| year=2000}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.epj.org/images/stories/news/2013/epj_d_1-02-13.pdf| title=Electron impact ionization cross sections of beryllium and beryllium hydrides| publisher=The European Physical Journal D| access-date=October 7, 2015}}</ref> Becker also researches the properties of basic atmospheric-pressure microplasmas and their use in environmental, biological, and biomedical applications.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://germanaccelerator.com/team/kurt-becker/| title=Kurt Becker| publisher=German Accelerator| access-date=October 7, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=http://academyofinventors.org/conference/docs/2014-program.pdf| title=2014 3rd Annual Congerence| publisher=National Academy of Inventors| access-date=October 7, 2015| archive-date=March 21, 2016| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160321202751/http://academyofinventors.org/conference/docs/2014-program.pdf| url-status=dead}}</ref> His research showed that unstable plasmas, which can be guided with a vacuum, become more stable when confined to less than 1mm, allowing for the manipulation of chemicals within.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://northsidefestival2012.sched.org/speaker/kurtbecker#.Vc5FM7JViko| title=Kurt Becker| publisher=Northside Festival| access-date=October 7, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=http://blogs.shu.edu/magazine/2013/04/giving-physics-a-good-name/| title=Giving Physics a Good Name| publisher=Seton Hall Magazine| access-date=October 7, 2015}}</ref> This research resulted in 7 patents and formed the basis of 2 startup companies, PlasmaSol and Plasmion.  PlasmaSol was sold to Stryker Instruments for $18,000,000 in 2005.

* H. Deutsch, F.X. Bronold, and K. Becker, "Calculations of Electron-Impact Ionization Cross Sections: Bottom-up Inductive vs. Top-down Deductive Approaches, Int. J. Mass Spectrom. 365/366, 128-39 (2014)
* K. Becker, O. Herskowitz, M.J. Kotch, E. Wheeler, J. Aloise, J. Byrd, and J.M. Peterson, "PowerBridgeNY:  A Cleantech Proof-of-Concept Center", Technology and Innovation 16(3-4), 215-222 (2014)
